title: Fractional physics-informed neural networks to model social media virality
summary: A segmented fractional physics-informed neural network modeled engagement trajectories for 348 X posts. It reconstructed 64% of held-out trajectories within the stated error threshold, versus 44% for the strongest of nine classical baselines. The result is limited to the sampled posts and does not establish causal social-media dynamics.
ai_technology: Fractional physics-informed neural network with symbolic regression
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: On 348 X posts, a four-segment teacher-forced model reconstructed 64% of held-out trajectories within the reported mean-squared-error threshold, versus 44% for the strongest of nine classical baselines. Synthetic experiments also tested recovery under clean and noisy observations.
evidence.unknown: The single-window model performed poorly on held-out trajectories; results concern sampled posts and do not establish causal mechanisms or general social-media dynamics.
evidence.ai_role: A fractional PINN learned temporal memory and nonlinear engagement dynamics; symbolic regression translated learned dynamics into equations.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
